statement: Samsung has locked up about 70% of its memory capacity under long-term agreements with customers including Microsoft, Nvidia and Google, with the agreements running through 2031.
why: Capacity committed under multi-year contracts to a handful of very large buyers is not available to the merchant market, so the pool of uncommitted HBM and DRAM supply keeps shrinking for everyone else.

impact.mechanism: Long-term agreements pre-allocate the majority of one of the three HBM suppliers' output to a few hyperscale and GPU customers, leaving smaller accelerator and cloud buyers dependent on a thin, expensive spot pool.

confidence.basis: Single secondary outlet (syndicated 24/7 Wall St. piece on Yahoo Finance); no Samsung filing or company statement fetched to corroborate the 70% figure.
